title: Stop prepending mise shims to the uwsm session PATH
head: 0e02c67027d8
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: Removing dynamic activation loses configured mise shim directories
leads.consequence: With MISE_SHIMS_DIR, MISE_DATA_DIR, XDG_DATA_HOME or mise's shims_dir setting pointing away from ~/.local/share/mise/shims, the uwsm environment still appends only the default directory. Previously mise activate bash --shims after the user override dynamically included the configured user shim directory (and, when it exists, the system shim directory); after removal the actual shims can be absent from the uwsm PATH, so direct graphical commands and user units cannot find mise-managed binaries unless another source adds their directory. This is conditional on such a configuration, not an assertion about stock installations.
leads.triage: already_in_opus_final; Opus runs F1-F3, C4; published as the opt-in mise setups note

leads.summary: Open PR #10552 would restore shims-first precedence in the same session
leads.consequence: If #10552's env-bootstrap and this change both merge, bootstrap explicitly moves ~/.local/share/mise/shims to the front on production installs, ahead of /usr/bin and ~/.local/bin. Deleting activation in 10-omarchy will no longer produce this PR's intended precedence. On a stock production install, a test using the merged installed bootstrap would fail its not-first assertion; the committed test, which reads whatever bootstrap is installed under /usr/share rather than the checkout version, need not fail in CI.
leads.triage: verified_not_published; coordinator confirmed #10552 open and touches env-bootstrap; author the author is on the opt-out registry, so no public reference

leads.summary: Missing or unreadable bootstrap now silently hides mise shims from graphical consumers
leads.consequence: If the guarded /usr/share/omarchy/default/bash/env-bootstrap is missing or unreadable while mise is still available (an incomplete or mismatched install), the old last line would still have activated mise shims; now the file falls through with no shim path and no error. Direct graphical commands that need a mise-only executable fail to find it. The package recipe installs both files in ordinary installs, so this specifically concerns partial installations or overrides.
leads.triage: already_in_opus_final_not_published; both files ship in omarchy-settings (Opus, Sol PKGBUILD); unrealistic install state

leads.summary: New test can pass with no shims, and does not verify the checkout's bootstrap
leads.consequence: The test checks only that the FIRST PATH component is not shims; it neither requires shims to exist nor requires /usr/bin and ~/.local/bin to precede shims. It sources the checkout 10-omarchy but this file sources the bootstrap from the absolute installed /usr/share path, not from the checkout, so it misses regressions or simultaneous changes to checkout bootstrap. It can report ok when no mise-managed command is available to a session.
leads.triage: already_in_opus_final; Opus mutants M1/M3; published as Optional test improvement

leads.summary: Open PR #8406 adds the same test filename and modifies the same env file
leads.consequence: Both branches add test/shell.d/uwsm-env-path-test.sh with different contents (add/add merge conflict), and edit the identical removal site in 10-omarchy. They need deliberate reconciliation: #8406 retains a mise activation fallback for an absent bootstrap and asserts shims occur exactly once and after /usr/bin; #13364 deletes the fallback and asserts only not-first. Simply selecting one new test discards coverage of the other's behaviour.
leads.triage: already_in_opus_final; coordinator verified via gh pr view file list and #8406 diff; published

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** the change produces the PATH order it describes, and no correctness issue was found in the two changed files. In a sandbox with real mise 2026.9.4, sourcing `10-omarchy` with `sh` (as uwsm does) and the repository's `env-bootstrap` gave:

```text
starting PATH: /usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin

base: <shims>:/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:<shims>:~/.local/bin
head:          /usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:<shims>:~/.local/bin
```

Running the same files through uwsm 0.26.7's own `prepare-env.sh` gave the same order. The duplicate comes from mise itself: current mise's `mise activate bash --shims` prepends the shims directory unless it is already first, even when `env-bootstrap` has already appended it. The new test fails on base and passes on head. The `dev-env-path`, `browser-env` and `editor-env` tests pass at head.

Also **Verified:** the tmux layouts that motivated 7e69c87 are unaffected, because they type commands into interactive panes where `mise activate bash` runs. Interactive terminals end with the same PATH on base and head. The quattro upgrade already neutralises this exact line in migrated `~/.config/uwsm/env` content, so no stale copy survives unless the user edited it.

### Desktop-launched processes now prefer system binaries over mise tools

Removing the line does more than drop a duplicate: the leading shims were what made mise versions win over same-named system binaries for everything started from the desktop without an interactive shell.

```text
command: ruby  (Omarchy base package, plus `omarchy-install-dev-env ruby` → mise use --global ruby@latest)

                          base              head
desktop session PATH      mise shim         /usr/bin/ruby
interactive terminal      mise Ruby         mise Ruby
```

The same applies to `python` and `python3` after `omarchy-install-dev-env python`. Interactive shells are unaffected because `mise activate bash` puts mise's tool directories first on both base and head. Processes that inherit the session PATH without an interactive shell, such as apps started from Hyprland or `uwsm-app` and systemd user units, resolve the system copy for any command they look up by name.

**Impact:** after this PR, a desktop-launched process and a terminal can resolve different Ruby or Python versions, where before both preferred mise. This matches the "appended so system binaries keep precedence" rule in `env-bootstrap` and #6632, so it may well be the intended outcome, but the PR description does not mention the flip.

**Suggested change:** state the precedence change in the PR description so the choice is explicit.

### Overlap with open PR #8406

#8406 changes the same line (it keeps `mise activate --shims` only when the shims are not already on PATH) and adds a test at the same path, `test/shell.d/uwsm-env-path-test.sh`. Its test is hermetic and asserts the shims appear once and after `/usr/bin`.

**Impact:** both PRs add `test/shell.d/uwsm-env-path-test.sh`, so whichever merges second hits an add/add conflict.

**Suggested change:** reconcile the two PRs (for example, one of them adopts the other's test).

### Optional test improvement

The test asserts only that the first PATH entry is not the shims directory. Two mutants of `10-omarchy` still pass: one that drops the `env-bootstrap` sourcing so the session has no shims at all, and one that inserts the shims second. The test is also not hermetic: `10-omarchy` sources the installed `/usr/share/omarchy/default/bash/env-bootstrap` by absolute path (and through it `/etc/omarchy.conf`), so it tests the host's bootstrap rather than the one in the tree, or no bootstrap at all on a machine without Omarchy. Testing a copy of `10-omarchy` whose bootstrap line points at a `sed` copy of the repository's `env-bootstrap` (with `/etc/omarchy.conf` redirected, as `test/shell.d/dev-env-path-test.sh` does for the bootstrap), and asserting that the shims appear exactly once and after `/usr/bin`, would close both gaps.

**Opt-in mise setups:** the removed line also added mise's command-wrappers directory and a system shim directory when present, and followed a relocated shims directory when `MISE_DATA_DIR` or `XDG_DATA_HOME` is set. `env-bootstrap` hardcodes only `~/.local/share/mise/shims`, so those opt-in setups lose them in the desktop session. Non-interactive SSH commands and `bash -lc` already have this limitation.

**Description note:** on a default install `env-bootstrap` appends `~/.local/bin` after the shims (see the head line above), so a binary linked into `~/.local/bin` is still shadowed by a same-named shim in the session unless the login PATH already puts `~/.local/bin` first. The zoxide overhead example also applies to non-interactive session processes only; interactive bash ends with the same PATH on base and head.

---

**Test scope:** source review of the PR, mise and uwsm, plus sandboxed runs of the PR test, test mutants, real mise 2026.9.4 and uwsm 0.26.7's `prepare-env.sh` with a synthetic home. No live desktop session was observed, and third-party editors that resolve their own shell environment were not tested.
